summary: Tarski's problems for free groups, planned on top of FreeGroupsAndLimitGroups (its layers FG1–FG11 are suppliers): formula classes and the alternating standard form over F(A) with the free lifting theorem (FO1); the parametrization theorem for arbitrary NTQ systems with correcting extensions, generic families of NTQ systems, and the fundamental-sequence infrastructure (strict and well-aligned sequences, canonical NTQ systems, sequences modulo subgroups) (FO2); MAX-equivalence, reducing quotients, algebraic solutions and the uniform bound on their number (FO4); induced NTQ systems, projective images, tight enveloping NTQ groups and configuration groups (FO3); the ∀∃-decision tree with its finiteness, correctness and the decidability of the ∀∃-theory, Sacerdote's rank independence and the computable bound (FO5); the parametric tree, the elimination of ∃∀∃-formulas level by level and the outer quantifier-elimination procedure with its termination measure (FO6); and Tarski's theorems: decidability of Th(F(A)), elementary equivalence of nonabelian free groups, the elementary embeddings F_k ≤ F_ℓ, closed surface groups of Euler characteristic ≤ −2, the classification of finitely generated models as extended hyperbolic towers, and negative controls (FO7). The proof route is Kharlampovich–Myasnikov's, in the corrected form of their 2012–2019 papers; Sela's route is recorded as the alternative, and the contested steps and the unread 2006 paper are recorded as gaps.

nodes.title: ∀∃- and ∃∀-formulas and the Boolean combinations of ∀∃-formulas
nodes.statement: For a first-order language L, free variables α and n bound variables, define on L.BoundedFormula α n three syntactic classes. (1) IsForallExists φ (a ∀∃-formula): the least class containing every existential formula (Mathlib's IsExistential: a block of ex over a quantifier-free formula) and closed under all; so φ = ∀x₁…∀xₖ∃y₁…∃yₘ θ with θ quantifier-free, k, m ≥ 0. (2) IsExistsForall φ (an ∃∀-formula): the least class containing every universal formula (Mathlib's IsUniversal) and closed under ex. (3) IsBoolCombAE φ: the least class containing ⊥ and every ∀∃-formula and closed under ∼, ⊓ and ⊔. The classes are syntactic. Because ∼(∀x∃y θ) is realized exactly where ∃x∀y ∼θ is, every ∃∀-formula is equivalent in every structure to the negation of a ∀∃-formula, so the Boolean combinations of ∃∀-formulas and of ∀∃-formulas define the same sets; the sources state quantifier elimination with either class (SELA-VI, HYP: ∀∃ / AE; QE-FREE: ∃∀).
proofSteps: Define IsForallExists and IsExistsForall as inductive predicates with two constructors each (base from Mathlib's IsExistential, respectively IsUniversal; closure under all, respectively ex).
Define IsBoolCombAE inductively with constructors falsum, of_isForallExists, not, inf, sup; ⊤ = ∼⊥ is then a member.

Prove the semantic duality: for θ quantifier-free, ∼(all…all (ex…ex θ)) and ex…ex (all…all ∼θ) have the same realizations (Mathlib's realize_not, realize_all, realize_ex), so every ∃∀-formula is equivalent in every structure to a member of IsBoolCombAE.
acceptance: A quantifier-free formula is ∀∃, ∃∀ and a Boolean combination of ∀∃-formulas.
ex (all θ) with θ atomic is ∃∀ but not ∀∃; all (ex (all θ)) is neither.

nodes.title: Equivalence of formulas over a group, and the sense of equivalence over a free group
nodes.statement: For an L-structure M, bounded formulas φ, ψ : L.BoundedFormula α n are equivalent over M (written φ ∼_M ψ) when φ.Realize v xs ↔ ψ.Realize v xs for all v : α → M and xs : Fin n → M. For the language of groups with coefficients carried by free variables (FG3: an L_A-formula with parameters P is a formula with free variables A ⊕ P, realized in a group G with coefficients c : A → G under Sum.elim c v), two L_A-formulas are equivalent over F(A) when they define the same subset of F(A)^P with c = FreeGroup.of; they are equivalent modulo a set T of sentences when every model of T realizes them at the same tuples (IFT §2.3, p. 5, writes Φ ∼_T Ψ). Equivalence over F(A) is equivalence modulo the complete theory Th_A(F(A)) of F(A) with its constants. Quantifier elimination over F(A) (FO1/qe-target, FO6, FO7) means equivalence over F(A) in this sense; the uniform statement for coefficient-free formulas over all nonabelian free groups of finite rank is FO7/uniform-qe.
proofSteps: Define EquivOver M φ ψ by the displayed biconditional; it is an equivalence relation and a congruence for ∼, ⊓, ⊔, all and ex by Mathlib's realize lemmas.
Relate it to the complete theory: for formulas (n = 0) with finitely many free variables, φ ∼_M ψ iff the universal closure iAlls of φ.iff ψ is in L.completeTheory M.
Relate it to definable sets: φ ∼_M ψ iff the sets {v | φ.Realize v} and {v | ψ.Realize v} coincide.
acceptance: Over the trivial group every formula is equivalent to ⊤ or ⊥.
Over F(a, b) the formula ∀y (x y = y x) is equivalent to x = 1.

nodes.title: The alternating standard form ∀X₁∃Y₁…∀X_k∃Y_k ⋁(S = 1 ∧ T ≠ 1)
nodes.statement: There is a computable map stdForm on (codes of) L_A-formulas with parameters P such that stdForm φ has the shape ∀X₁∃Y₁…∀X_k∃Y_k ⋁_{i=1}^{r}(S_i = 1 ∧ T_i ≠ 1), with k ≥ 0 and tuples X_j, Y_j possibly empty, in one of two forms. (1) General form: each S_i = 1 is a finite (possibly empty) system of equations and each T_i ≠ 1 a finite (possibly empty) system of inequations, every component a word in X ∪ Y ∪ P ∪ A, and φ ∼_T stdForm φ for T the group axioms (equivalent in every group with coefficients; IFT §2.3). If φ is coefficient-free, so is its general form. (2) Merged form: over the class of torsion-free nonabelian CSA groups satisfying Vaught's condition and containing non-commuting coefficients a, b ∈ A, in particular over F(A) with |A| ≥ 2, each S_i and each T_i is a single word, computed effectively from the general form (IFT Corollaries 3, 5, Lemma 5 and Corollary 7); the merging introduces the constants a, b, so the merged form of a coefficient-free formula is not coefficient-free. The number k of ∀∃-blocks is the block count used as the termination measure in FO6.
hypotheses: Merged form (2) only: the group is torsion-free, nonabelian, CSA, satisfies Vaught's condition and contains non-commuting coefficients a, b ∈ A (every nonabelian free group F(A) with |A| ≥ 2 does).
proofSteps: Apply Mathlib's toPrenex and realize_toPrenex (groups are nonempty).
Group equal adjacent quantifiers into blocks and insert empty blocks (fictitious quantifiers over unused variables) so that the prefix alternates and starts with ∀ and ends with ∃.

Rewrite the matrix with FG3/quantifier-free-normal-form as a finite disjunction of systems (the general form (1)); over F(A) merge each system into one equation and one inequation with IFT Corollaries 3, 5 and Lemma 5 (planned in FG7/positive-normal-form; the merged form (2)).
Each step is a primitive recursive operation on codes (FG3/syntax-operations-computable).
acceptance: ∀x∃y([x, y] = 1) is already in standard form with k = 1.
∃y (y² = a) gets k = 1 with X₁ empty; a quantifier-free formula gets k = 0.
For coefficient-free φ the general form (1) is coefficient-free, while the merged form (2) contains the constants a, b of the Malcev and commutator encodings.

nodes.title: Free lifts of a sentence: formal witnesses in F[X]
nodes.statement: Let F = F(A) and let φ = ∀x₁∃y₁…∀x_k∃y_k φ₀ be an L_A-sentence in standard form (FO1/standard-form, blocks written as single variables for brevity), with φ₀ quantifier-free. For i ≤ k write F[x₁,…,x_i] = F ∗ F(x₁,…,x_i) (FG5/coefficient-free-product). F freely lifts φ when there are words q₁(x₁) ∈ F[x₁], q₂(x₁, x₂) ∈ F[x₁, x₂], …, q_k(x₁,…,x_k) ∈ F[x₁,…,x_k] such that φ₀(x₁, q₁(x₁), …, x_k, q_k(x₁,…,x_k)) holds in the group F[X] = F ∗ F(x₁,…,x_k) with the x_i as constants. The tuple (q₁,…,q_k) is a free lift; the i-th witness depends only on the first i universal variables. nodes.title: Free lifting theorem: every true sentence is freely lifted
nodes.statement: Let F = F(A) be a nonabelian free group of finite rank. Every L_A-sentence φ in standard form (FO1/standard-form) that is true in F is freely lifted by F (FO1/free-lift): there are words q_i(x₁,…,x_i) ∈ F[x₁,…,x_i] with φ₀(x₁, q₁, …, x_k, q_k) true in F[X]. Moreover the free lift can be chosen so that, for Merzljakov's tuple g₁,…,g_k of FG7/merzljakov-theorem, q_i(g₁,…,g_i) is a witness h_i in F.
hypotheses: F nonabelian of finite rank; φ true in F; φ in standard form.
proofSteps: Write φ₀ as ⋁(U_i = 1 ∧ V_i ≠ 1) (FO1/standard-form); choose the elements g₁,…,g_k of Merzljakov's proof (FG7/merzljakov-theorem) and witnesses h₁,…,h_k in F with φ₀(g, h) true.
For the disjunct true at (g, h), Merzljakov's argument gives q_i ∈ F[x₁,…,x_i] with U(x, q(x)) = 1 in F[X] and h_i = q_i(g).
V(x, q(x)) ≠ 1 in F[X], because its image under the specialization x ↦ g is V(g, h) ≠ 1.
Hence the disjunct, and so φ₀, holds in F[X] at (x, q(x)).
acceptance: ∀x∃y (y ≠ 1 ∧ [x, y] = 1) is true in F and freely lifted by y = x.
Merzljakov's theorem is the positive case (no inequations).

nodes.title: Positive sentences: rank independence and truth in every group
nodes.statement: A positive coefficient-free sentence φ = ∀x₁∃y₁…∀x_k∃y_k (S(X, Y) = 1) (no constants) holds in one nonabelian free group of finite rank iff it holds in all of them, iff it holds in every group. For positive sentences with constants from A the truth value over F(A) is decided by FG7/positive-theory-decider; that decider and Merzljakov's theorem are FreeGroupsAndLimitGroups FG7 targets and are consumed here, not restated.
hypotheses: φ positive (no inequations) and coefficient-free.
proofSteps: If φ holds in F_n (n ≥ 2), the free lifting theorem (FO1/free-lifting-theorem) gives q_i ∈ F_n ∗ F(x₁,…,x_i) with φ₀(x, q(x)) true in F_n ∗ F(X); since φ₀ is positive, some conjunction of equations S_j(x, q(x)) = 1 holds in F_n ∗ F(X). (The single-equation encoding of FG7/positive-normal-form is not used here: it introduces the constants a, b, which a homomorphism to G need not preserve.)

For any group G and g ∈ G^X, the homomorphism F_n ∗ F(X) → G that is trivial on F_n and sends x ↦ g maps each S_j(x, q(x)) to S_j(g, q̄(g)) = 1, because S_j has no constants; the witnesses q̄_i(g) depend only on g₁,…,g_i, so φ holds in G.
Conversely a sentence true in every group is true in every free group.

nodes.title: ∀∃-quantifier elimination: the target property, plain and effective
nodes.statement: For an L-structure M: M has ∀∃-quantifier elimination (HasAEQE M) when for every α, n and φ : L.BoundedFormula α n there is ψ with IsBoolCombAE ψ (FO1/quantifier-classes) and φ ∼_M ψ (FO1/equivalence-over). For the free group F(A) with constants (L_A-formulas with parameters P, FG3), effective ∀∃-quantifier elimination means a computable function on the FG3 codes of L_A-formulas returning such ψ with the same parameters. This is the property the sources prove for F(A) (QE-FREE Theorem 1 with ∃∀; HYP Theorem 1 for torsion-free hyperbolic groups, Γ = F; SELA-VI Theorem 1, non-effective), the endpoint of FO6. It concerns formulas with parameters: restricted to sentences it would hold for every structure, since a sentence is equivalent over M to ⊤ or ⊥.
proofSteps: Define HasAEQE M as the displayed ∀∃ statement.
Define the effective version as the existence of a computable map on the Primcodable type of codes of formulas (FG3/effective-encoding) with the two properties.
Prove that it is invariant under elementary equivalence: if φ ∼_M ψ for formulas then the universal closure of φ.iff ψ lies in Th(M), hence holds in every N ≅[L] M.
acceptance: The trivial group has ∀∃-quantifier elimination.
A structure with effective ∀∃-elimination and a decidable ∀∃-theory has a decidable theory (FO7).

nodes.title: Strict fundamental sequences of solutions
nodes.statement: Let S(X, A) = 1 be a finite system over F = F(A) and G = F_{R(S)}. A fundamental sequence (fundamental set of solutions) is the set of F-homomorphisms G → F of the form π₀ σ₁ π₁ ⋯ σ_{k−1} π_{k−1} φ₀ attached to one branch G → G₁ → ⋯ → G_k = F(Y) ∗ F of a Makanin–Razborov (Hom-) diagram (FG10/makanin-razborov-diagram): π_i fixed proper F-epimorphisms between fully residually free groups, σ_i canonical automorphisms of G_i (generated by Dehn twists along edges of the Grushko-then-abelian-JSJ decomposition of G_i, automorphisms of QH vertex groups fixing peripheral structure, and automorphisms of abelian vertex groups fixing edge groups), φ₀ an arbitrary F-homomorphism F(Y) ∗ F → F. It is strict when, for every 1 ≤ i < k: (1) π_i maps every non-abelian vertex group of G_i to a non-abelian subgroup; (2) π_i is injective on rigid vertex groups, on edge groups and on the subgroups generated by images of edge groups in abelian vertex groups; (3) π_i is injective on the envelope ⟨R, Is(η₁(E₁)), …, Is(η_m(E_m))⟩ of each rigid vertex group R, where E_j are the edges from R to abelian vertex groups A_j and Is(·) is the isolator (least direct factor containing it) in A_j; (4) distinct Grushko factors of G_i go to distinct free factors of G_{i+1}. Property (3) is the correction the authors made to KM06, whose fundamental sequences satisfied only (1)–(2).
proofSteps: Represent a fundamental sequence by a branch of an FG10 diagram together with the canonical automorphism groups Q_v at its vertices (finite generating lists of automorphisms, FG10/frf-basic-algorithms).
State conditions (1)–(4) as predicates on the branch data, using the abelian JSJ decompositions of FG10 and isolators in free abelian vertex groups.
The set of homomorphisms of the sequence is the image of the composite map from Q_{v₁} × ⋯ × Q_{v_{k−1}} × Hom_F(F(Y) ∗ F, F).
acceptance: For S = ∅ (G = F[X]) the one-vertex sequence G = F(X) ∗ F with φ₀ arbitrary is strict.
A sequence whose π₁ kills an edge group of G₁ is not strict.

nodes.title: The canonical NTQ system of a strict fundamental sequence
nodes.statement: To a strict fundamental sequence G → G₁ → ⋯ → G_k = F(Y) ∗ F (FO2/strict-fundamental-sequence) one assigns, bottom-up, an NTQ system (FG8/ntq-system) whose coordinate group N₁ contains the image of G. At level k − 1, for each free factor of G_{k−1} with abelian JSJ decomposition D: (Step 1) for each edge of D between rigid vertex groups extend the centralizer of the image of its edge group in G_k by a new letter, adding commutation relations so that the result H₁ is commutative transitive; (Step 2) for each non-cyclic abelian vertex group A = Is(A_e) × A₀ extend the centralizer of the image of Is(A_e) by A₀ (equations [y_p, y_q] = 1, [y_p, d̄_j] = 1), identifying abelian vertex groups whose images become conjugate into one abelian subgroup; (Step 3) for each QH vertex group with relation ∏[x_i, y_i] p₁⋯p_m = 1 add a quadratic equation ∏[x_i, y_i] c₁^{z₁}⋯c_{m−1}^{z_{m−1}} c_m = 1 with the images c_j of the boundary elements as coefficients. The free product over the factors is the level-(k−1) group; repeating upwards gives N₁ = F_{R(W)} with W NTQ, and G embeds in N₁ when the sequence is strict. The construction is effective (finite presentations of the N_i and generators of their canonical automorphism groups).
proofSteps: Work level by level from the bottom; at each level treat the Grushko factors separately and take the free product.
Steps 1–3 as in the statement; check commutation transitivity after each extension by the conjugacy and centralizer algorithms of FG10/frf-basic-algorithms.

Embedding of G: strictness (conditions (2)–(3)) makes the rigid part embed in the iterated centralizer extension, the abelian vertex groups embed through Step 2 and the QH vertex groups through Step 3; FG8/ntq-coordinate-group gives that each level is an NTQ group.
acceptance: For a one-level sequence whose G₁ is a QH-vertex group over F, the canonical NTQ system is a single regular quadratic equation over F.

nodes.title: Well-aligned fundamental sequences: the first and second restrictions
nodes.statement: A strict fundamental sequence for an irreducible system S = 1 over F, with NTQ system Q = (Q₁(X₁,…,X_n) = 1, …, Q_n(X_n) = 1) adjoined with free variables t₁,…,t_k and π_i : F_{R(Q_i,…,Q_n)} ∗ F(t₁,…,t_{k_{i−1}}) → F_{R(Q_{i+1},…,Q_n)} ∗ F(t₁,…,t_{k_i}), is well aligned when it satisfies: (First restriction) for every MQH vertex group Q of every level, with the free decomposition π(Q) = K₁ ∗ ⋯ ∗ K_p ∗ ⟨t_{j₁}⟩ ∗ ⋯ inherited from the reduced free decomposition of the next level, the surface Σ of Q is cut along a maximal family of disjoint non-homotopic simple closed curves mapped to 1 and realizing that decomposition; each piece attached to a rigid vertex group has no further essential simple closed curve mapped to 1 after capping the boundary components mapped to 1, and each piece not attached to a rigid vertex group caps to a closed surface mapped onto a free group of maximal rank. (Second restriction) at every level: images of distinct abelian free factors are distinct free factors of F(t_{k_{i−1}+1},…,t_{k_i}); likewise for surface-group factors; free variables of quadratic equations correspond to new t's and the images of their coefficients are not conjugate into the new free factor; distinct free factors go to distinct free factors. Here k_i is the number of free variables added at level i, so that the free factor at level i + 1 has the k₁ + ⋯ + k_i variables of the levels above it (QE-FREE writes it F(t₁,…,t_{k_i}), sourceIssue E12); the free variables new at level i are the k_i variables written t_{k_{i−1}+1},…,t_{k_i} in the restrictions above. The dimension of the sequence is k₁ + ⋯ + k_n, the total number of free variables, equal to the rank of the free factor of the terminal level.

nodes.title: Generic families of solutions of an NTQ system (all level types)

nodes.title: Normalization of an NTQ system along a fundamental sequence
nodes.statement: Let U(X) = 1 be an NTQ system over F with a fundamental sequence V̄(U). nodes.title: Correcting extensions and correcting normalizing embeddings
nodes.statement: Let U(X) = 1 be a normalized NTQ system (FO2/normalized-ntq) and W(X, Y) = 1 an equation (or W = 1 ∧ W₁ ≠ 1). Starting from the bottom, each centralizer-extending level U_com(X_i) = 1 is replaced by finitely many systems Ū_com(X_i) = 1 obtained from the periodic structures of the solution tree T_sol of W = 1 ∧ U = 1 with parameters X_i,…,X_n (FG7 generalized equations): each replacement extends the relevant centralizer by a larger free abelian group containing the old one with finite index, with embeddings φ_k between the abelian vertex groups. This yields the finite set C_W(U) of NTQ systems Ū_j with embeddings F_{R(U)} ↪ F_{R(Ū_j)}; combined with normalization, NCW(U) := C_W(U*) with the correcting normalizing embeddings θ_j : F_{R(U)} → F_{R(Ū_j)}. Proceed upward; the result is a finite set C_W(U*) with embeddings θ_j; each Ū_j is NTQ and the abelian size is preserved.

nodes.title: Parametrization theorem (implicit function theorem for arbitrary NTQ systems)
nodes.statement: Let U(X, A) = 1 be an NTQ system over F = F(A) with a fundamental sequence of solutions V̄(U), and suppose Φ = ∀X(U(X) = 1 → ∃Y(W(X, Y, A) = 1 ∧ W₁(X, Y, A) ≠ 1)) is true in F. Then for every Ū_i ∈ NCW(U) (FO2/correcting-extension, relative to W) and its correcting normalizing embedding θ_i : F_{R(U)} → F_{R(Ū_i)}, the formula ∃Y(W(X^{θ_i}, Y, A) = 1 ∧ W₁(X^{θ_i}, Y, A) ≠ 1) holds in F_{R(Ū_i)}; this can be verified effectively and a solution Y found effectively. Furthermore every fundamental solution φ : F_{R(U)} → F factors as φ = θ_i ψ with ψ a fundamental solution of some Ū_i.

proofSteps: Normalize U; on regular quadratic levels the generic families of FG11/generic-families give complete lifts (FG11/ift-regular-quadratic).

On centralizer-extending levels, the solutions of W over the generic family are controlled by the periodic structures of T_sol; the correcting extensions adjoin exactly the roots those structures require, so the lift exists in each Ū_i (IFT §7.6).
Combine level by level as in FG11/ift-regular-ntq; effectiveness: enumerate candidate Y and test with the word problem in F_{R(Ū_i)} (FG10/frf-basic-algorithms-correct), termination by existence.
The factorization statement is FO2/correcting-extension (correctingExt_cover).
acceptance: For U regular and without U_com levels this is FG11/ift-regular-ntq.
For U empty this is the free lifting theorem with one block (FO1/free-lifting-theorem).

nodes.statement: Let F ≤ H ≤ K be finitely generated fully residually free groups (H given by generators, K by a finite presentation). nodes.title: Reducing quotients and special homomorphisms

nodes.title: MAX-equivalence of homomorphisms (fractional Dehn twists)
nodes.statement: Let G be a fully residually free group with F ≤ G and D an abelian JSJ decomposition of G modulo a family K of subgroups. (a) For an elementary splitting S of G corresponding to an edge of D, G = A ∗_C B or G = ⟨A, t | c^t = c′ (c ∈ C)⟩ with F ≤ A, and an F-homomorphism ψ : G → F with ψ(C) ≤ ⟨c₀⟩ (a maximal cyclic subgroup of F), and d ∈ ⟨c₀⟩: ψ_d agrees with ψ on A and is ψ(b)^d on B (amalgam), or sends t to dψ(t) (HNN); ∼_S relates ψ and ψ_d. (b) For an abelian vertex group M = M₁ × M₂ of D (M₁ the least direct summand containing the edge groups, M₂ with fixed basis g₁,…,g_s), G is an extension of the centralizer of M₁ in G′ (the fundamental group of D without M₂) by M₂; for θ with θ(M) ≤ ⟨c₀⟩ and d ∈ ⟨c₀⟩^s, θ_d agrees with θ on G′ and sends g_i to d_i θ(g_i); ∼_M relates θ and θ_d. (c) ∼_AE is the equivalence relation generated by equivalence under canonical automorphisms, all ∼_M and all ∼_S. (d) φ ∼_MAX ψ when there is θ with φ ∼_AE θ and θ agreeing with ψ up to conjugation on the fundamental group of every connected component of D with its QH vertex groups removed.
proofSteps: Define ψ_d and θ_d explicitly on generators adapted to D; they are homomorphisms because d commutes with ψ(C), respectively with θ(M).

Define ∼_AE as an EqvGen closure and ∼_MAX as in (d); prove that ∼_MAX is an equivalence relation (the sources speak of MAX-classes). Symmetry and transitivity need, besides ∼_AE being an equivalence, that the twists generating ∼_AE are compatible with agreement up to conjugation on the non-QH components: a twist ψ_d or θ_d is determined by the values on the edge and abelian vertex groups, which lie in those components; this compatibility is part of the node's proof.
acceptance: For K rigid modulo H with D trivial, ∼_MAX is equality on F-homomorphisms.
All F-homomorphisms of ⟨F(a, b), t | [t, a]⟩ to F are ∼_MAX-equivalent.

nodes.title: Complete reducing systems
nodes.statement: Let K, H be as in FO4/reducing-quotient. A complete reducing system for K (modulo H) is a finite list of reducing quotients K/R(r₁), …, K/R(r_s) of K, each given by finitely many extra relations r_i and the NTQ systems of its fundamental sequences modulo H, such that every homomorphism K → F that factors through some reducing quotient is ∼_MAX-equivalent (FO4/max-equivalence) to one that factors through one of the K/R(r_i). A homomorphism K → F is reducing when its ∼_MAX-class contains a solution factoring through one of these NTQ systems.

Define the predicate IsReducingHom through ∼_MAX-classes.
acceptance: If K has no reducing quotient, the empty list is a complete reducing system.
A complete reducing system stays complete after adding further reducing quotients.

nodes.statement: Let K be a finitely generated fully residually free group without a sufficient splitting modulo a finitely generated subgroup H (given by a finite presentation and generators). A complete reducing system for K modulo H (FO4/complete-reducing-system), with the NTQ systems of its members modulo H, exists and can be found effectively.

nodes.title: Uniform bound on the number of MAX-classes of algebraic solutions
nodes.statement: Let H, K be finitely generated fully residually free groups with F ≤ H ≤ K and K without a sufficient splitting modulo H, and D an abelian JSJ decomposition of K modulo H (possibly trivial). There is N = N(K, H) such that for every F-homomorphism φ : H → F there are at most N pairwise non-∼_MAX-equivalent algebraic homomorphisms K → F extending φ. (Its effective computation is FO5/effective-bound.)
hypotheses: F ≤ H ≤ K f.g. fully residually free; K without sufficient splitting modulo H.
proofSteps: Suppose not: a sequence φ_n with more and more non-equivalent algebraic extensions.

Pass to a convergent sequence of extensions; by equational Noetherianity (FG5) and the descending chain condition on limit-group quotients (FG8), the limit factors through a proper quotient of K or gives a splitting of K modulo H.

A proper quotient makes almost all extensions reducing or special; a splitting would be sufficient or would make them MAX-equivalent: contradiction (KM06 §11 via generalized equations with intervals labelled by the generators of H).
acceptance: N(⟨F ∗ ⟨p⟩, x | x² = p⟩, F ∗ ⟨p⟩) = 1 (square roots are unique in F).

nodes.title: Size, abelian size, Kurosh rank and the complexity of a fundamental sequence
nodes.statement: For a QH vertex group Q with surface S_Q, size(Q) = (genus of S_Q, |χ(S_Q)|). For an abelian decomposition D of a freely indecomposable group, the regular size size(D) is the tuple of sizes of its MQH vertex groups in decreasing order, compared left-lexicographically; the abelian size ab(D) is the sum of the ranks of the abelian vertex groups minus the sum of the ranks of the edge groups of the edges at them (for NTQ systems: the sum over levels of the ranks of abelian vertex groups minus the ranks of their direct summands containing the edge groups with finite index). For a (block-)fundamental sequence V_fund, the Kurosh rank is dim(V_fund) + factors(V_fund), where dim is the rank of the free group of the terminal level (FO2/well-aligned) and factors is the number of freely indecomposable non-cyclic terminal factors (present only for sequences modulo subgroups). The complexity is Cmplx(V_fund) = (Kurosh rank, regular size, ab), compared left-lexicographically; it takes values in a well-ordered set.
proofSteps: Define size(Q) from the Euler characteristic and genus of the surface of Q (FG6).

Define size(D), ab(D), the Kurosh rank and Cmplx as tuples of natural numbers with the lexicographic order; finite tuples of bounded length under the lexicographic order of decreasing-sorted tuples are well-ordered, which is the termination measure of FO3/induced-ntq-terminates, FO5/ae-tree-finite and FO6/true-level-two.
acceptance: The empty system has complexity (|X|, (), 0).
A once-punctured torus vertex has size (1, 1).

nodes.title: Induced NTQ systems and induced fundamental sequences
nodes.statement: Let S = 1 be an NTQ system over F with levels F_i = F_{R(S_i,…,S_n)}, fixed F_{i+1}-homomorphisms π_i : F_i → F_{i+1} (F_{n+1} a free product of F and a free group), a well-aligned fundamental sequence (FO2/well-aligned), and K a finitely generated (F-)subgroup of F_{R(S)}. Assume F_{R(S)} freely indecomposable modulo F and let D be the splitting of the top level. The induced NTQ system Q = 1 is obtained by: taking the induced splitting D_K of K and its free factors K₁ ∗ ⋯ ∗ K_k; enlarging K₁ by finitely many elements of abelian vertex groups of F_{R(S)} (chosen in the complements A₂ of isolators and corrected to die on the next level) so that non-QH non-abelian subgroups conjugate into the same subgroup of D are joined; adding conjugating elements so that each punctured surface of the refined decomposition is attached to a unique rigid subgroup and all rigid subgroups mapped to the same free factor of the next level are conjugate into one subgroup (giving K̃₁ with π₁(K) = π₁(K̃₁)); doing the same for each free factor of π₁(K) ∩ ⟨X₂,…,X_n⟩ and down all levels (giving H₁); and iterating with H₁ in place of K until H_i = H_{i+1}. The result is an NTQ system Q with K ≤ F_{R(Q)} ≤ F_{R(S)}, levels and canonical automorphisms induced from those of S, each QH subgroup of finite index in a QH subgroup of S, the image of the top j levels of F_{R(Q)} at level j + 1 contained in the image of K there; the induced fundamental sequence contains every solution of K factoring through the given sequence of S. The same construction is made modulo a subgroup.
proofSteps: Compute the induced splitting D_K (FG4/induced-splitting) and its Grushko factors (FG4/kurosh-grushko) with the algorithms of FG10.
Perform the enlargement steps level by level from the top; each added element is found by the conjugacy and centralizer algorithms of FG10/frf-basic-algorithms.
Iterate; termination is FO3/induced-ntq-terminates.
Read off the levels, the maps between levels (restrictions of the π_i) and the canonical automorphisms (restrictions of those of S).
acceptance: For K = F_{R(S)} the induced system is S.
For K = F the induced system is empty.

nodes.title: Termination of the induced-NTQ enlargement
nodes.statement: In the construction of FO3/induced-ntq the iteration K ⊆ H₁ ⊆ H₂ ⊆ ⋯ stabilizes after finitely many steps: if H_i ≠ H_{i+1} there is a level j such that the decompositions at all levels above j are unchanged and at level j one of the following decreases, in this priority: the number of free factors of the free decomposition at level j, the number of edges and vertices of the induced decomposition at level j, the size (regular size, then abelian size) of that decomposition. The resulting construction is algorithmic.
hypotheses: S NTQ with a well-aligned fundamental sequence; K finitely generated.
proofSteps: Compare the decompositions of H_i and H_{i+1} level by level from the top; the first level where they differ exhibits one of the three decreases, because enlargement only joins vertex groups or replaces QH subgroups by subgroups of finite index in larger ones.
The triples (free factors, edges + vertices, size) are compared lexicographically level by level; they lie in a well-ordered set (FO3/complexity), so the iteration stops.
acceptance: For K already equal to its enlargement the iteration stops at once.

nodes.title: Projective images of a subgroup along a (block-)NTQ system
nodes.statement: Let N be the coordinate group of an NTQ (or block-NTQ) system with levels N = N₁ → N₂ → ⋯ → N_m, the maps being the fixed homomorphisms π_i of a fundamental sequence (retractions in the completed sequence). For a finitely generated subgroup G ≤ N (more generally a homomorphism G → N), its projective image at level i is G^{(i)} := (π_{i−1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ π₁)(G) ≤ N_i, with the induced epimorphism G → G^{(i)}. The level of collapse of G is the least i with G → G^{(i)} not injective (a proper quotient), if any. Given finite presentations, G^{(i)} is computable (finite presentation of a finitely generated subgroup of a fully residually free group) and whether G → G^{(i)} is proper is decidable.

A finite presentation of G^{(i)} and the properness test use the algorithms for finitely generated subgroups of fully residually free groups (FG10/frf-basic-algorithms: finite presentations of subgroups, injectivity of homomorphisms).

nodes.title: The image of G at the terminal level is a proper quotient
nodes.statement: In the first step of the ∀∃-procedure (FO5/ae-tree), let G = F_{R(U₀)}, R₁,…,R_s the images of the free factors of ⟨X₂,…,X_n⟩, and c a fundamental sequence for G₁ modulo R₁,…,R_s whose dimension is less than k₁ or whose top NTQ level differs from S₁ = 1, with only homomorphisms minimal with respect to R₁,…,R_s. Then the projective image G_t of G at the terminal level t of c is a proper quotient of G, unless G is free; the level p at which the image first becomes proper is found effectively.
hypotheses: c consists of homomorphisms minimal with respect to R₁,…,R_s, which are non-trivial.
proofSteps: Suppose G_t ≅ G; the abelian JSJ decomposition D_t of H_t induces one of G in which rigid subgroups and edge groups are elliptic.
A free factor P_i of H_t then carries a decomposition induced from D_t, so the homomorphisms could be shortened by canonical automorphisms of P_i modulo the R_j conjugate into it.
This contradicts minimality modulo R₁,…,R_s (FO2/fundamental-sequences-modulo); hence G_t is a proper quotient, and FO3/projective-images finds the first proper level.

nodes.title: Tight enveloping NTQ groups and fundamental sequences
nodes.statement: Let G = F_{R(U)}, W(X₁,…,X_n) = 1 the canonical NTQ system of a branch of T_CE(F_{R(U)}) (FO2/canonical-embedding-tree) with top level S₁, P = 1 a system with coefficients in F_{R(W)} solvable in an extension of F_{R(W)}, and F_{R(L₁)} the NTQ group of a well-aligned fundamental sequence c(L₁) for P = 1 modulo the non-cyclic free factors of the second level ⟨X₂,…,X_n⟩ of F_{R(W)}, with G ≤ F_{R(L₁)}. The tight enveloping fundamental sequence TEnv(G; L₁) and its NTQ group are obtained from the induced NTQ group Ind(G) (FO3/induced-ntq) by repeating the adjustment until it stabilizes: (b) add, top to bottom, QH subgroups of F_{R(L₁)} meeting the image at level i + 1 in a subgroup of finite index and having fewer free variables than that intersection; (c) add edge groups of abelian vertex groups meeting Ind(G) when this does not increase the Kurosh rank; (d) add, bottom to top, QH subgroups without free variables that meet Ind(G) and an adjacent vertex group, when this decreases the Kurosh rank; (e) add elements conjugating distinct QH (or abelian vertex) subgroups of Ind(G) into one QH subgroup of F_{R(L₁)} when this decreases the Kurosh rank; (f) add to each non-cyclic free factor of the image at each level the abelian vertex and edge groups it meets. The construction is algorithmic, and the bound of KM06 Lemma 28 is computable.
proofSteps: Start from Ind(G) (FO3/induced-ntq), which does not increase the Kurosh rank.

Apply (b)–(f) in order; each step needs intersections of conjugates of QH subgroups of two NTQ groups and the rank of solution sets of quadratic systems, both computable (FG10/frf-basic-algorithms, FG6).
Repeat the adjustment until no step applies; each application either keeps the Kurosh rank and adds a subgroup of bounded type or decreases the Kurosh rank, so the repetition stops.
acceptance: If G = F_{R(L₁)} the tight envelope is c(L₁) itself.
The Kurosh rank of TEnv(G; L₁) does not exceed that of c(L₁).

nodes.title: Tight envelopes do not increase complexity (reorganization of the enveloping system)
nodes.statement: Let G ≤ F_{R(W)} and L₁ = 1 be as in FO3/tight-enveloping, the family of simple closed curves of each QH subgroup of S₁ mapped to 1 at the next level being compatible with the splittings induced from c(L₁). Then the Kurosh rank of TEnv(G; L₁) is at most the Kurosh rank of the fundamental sequence for S₁ = 1 modulo the free factors of ⟨X₂,…,X_n⟩. If they are equal, L₁ can be reorganized (moving stable QH subgroups down) into a well-aligned system L₂ = 1 with the same solutions from the fundamental sequences, through which every homomorphism of G factoring through c(L₁) also factors, and with size(TEnv(G; L₂)) ≤ size(S₁); if moreover all parameters (Kurosh rank, size, abelian rank, rank) agree, TEnv(G; L₂) has one level and the same abelian decomposition as S₁. The same holds for H ≤ F_{R(W)} with TEnv(H; S₁) in place of S₁.
hypotheses: Compatibility of the curve families as stated.
proofSteps: Compare the QH subgroups of TEnv(G; L₁) with those of S₁ through the surfaces and the compatible families of simple closed curves.
In the equality case, move stable QH subgroups (those mapped onto QH subgroups of the same size) down to a single level as in KM06 §7.3, obtaining L₂.
The size and abelian-rank comparisons follow from the finite-index inclusions of QH subgroups (FO3/induced-ntq).
acceptance: If G = F_{R(W)} and L₁ = W, equality holds and TEnv has one level.

nodes.title: Certificates and configuration groups
nodes.statement: Fix parameters P, an irreducible system U₁(P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾) = 1 with F_{R(U₁)} without sufficient splitting modulo ⟨P, Z⟩, systems V_{2,s}(P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾, Z₁⁽²⁾) = 1 (s = 1,…,t) with coordinate groups without sufficient splitting modulo ⟨P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾⟩, systems U_{2,m}(P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾, Z₁⁽²⁾, Z⁽²⁾) = 1, finitely many next-level systems V_{3,s}, and widths i₁,…,i_t. A certificate of level 2 and width i = i₁ + ⋯ + i_t for a value P̄ is a tuple (P̄, Z̄, Z̄⁽¹⁾, Z̄₁^{(2,j,s)}, Z̄^{(2,j,s)})_{j ≤ i_s, s ≤ t} such that: (1) (P̄, Z̄, Z̄⁽¹⁾) is an algebraic solution of U₁ (FO4/algebraic-solution), each (…, Z̄₁^{(2,j,s)}) an algebraic solution of V_{2,s} and each (…, Z̄^{(2,j,s)}) an algebraic solution of U_{2,m_s}; (2) the Z̄₁^{(2,j,s)}, j ≤ i_s, are pairwise not ∼_MAX-equivalent (FO4/max-equivalence); (3) for each of the finitely many values of Z₁⁽²⁾, the fundamental sequences of V_{2,s} are contained in the union of those of U_{2,m_s} for the values Z^{(2,j,s)}; (4) there is no further algebraic solution Z₁^{(2, i_s+1, s)} of V_{2,s} not ∼_MAX-equivalent to these; (5) (P̄, Z̄, Z̄⁽¹⁾) satisfies no proper equation that forces V_i(P̄, Z̄, X) = 1 for every X; (6) no (…, Z̄₁^{(2,1,s)}, Z̄^{(2,1,s)}) extends to a solution of a V_{3,s}. Adding root variables Q for the primitive roots of the images of the edge groups and abelian vertex groups of the relative JSJ decompositions of the F_{R(V_{2,s})}, the configuration groups are the fully residually free groups H discriminated by families of certificates factoring through one initial fundamental sequence of level 2 and width i modulo ⟨P⟩.
proofSteps: Encode certificates as solutions of a finite system of equations and inequations in the variables P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾, Z₁^{(2,j,s)}, Z^{(2,j,s)}, Q, with conditions (1)–(6) expressed through the complete reducing systems (FO4/reducing-quotients-effective), the twist parameters of FO4/max-class-count-definable and the systems V_{3,s}.

A configuration group is a maximal fully residually free quotient discriminated by a family of certificates through one initial fundamental sequence (FG8: every family of homomorphisms factors through finitely many maximal fully residually free quotients).
acceptance: With t = 0 the conditions reduce to (1) and (5) for U₁, and the configuration groups are the groups discriminated by algebraic solutions of U₁.
Widths are bounded by the bound N of FO4/algebraic-solution-bound for each V_{2,s}.

nodes.title: Finiteness and computability of configurations
nodes.statement: With the data of FO3/configuration-group: (1) there are only finitely many initial fundamental sequences of level 2 (finitely many widths, and finitely many sequences for each width), because the widths are bounded by FO4/algebraic-solution-bound; (2) for each configuration group H = F_{R(W)} with generators P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾, Z₁^{(2,j,s)}, Z^{(2,j,s)}, Q, the terminal group of each fundamental sequence for H modulo P can be found effectively, although no defining system W is given in advance; (3) hence the initial fundamental sequences for Z of level 2 and width i can be constructed effectively; (4) for each such sequence and each P̄ through it admitting a certificate, either there is a generic family of certificates in the sequence (depth 1), or every certificate extends by a further Z₁^{(2, i_s+1, s)} through one of the finitely many groups H_surplus with that extra variable reducing or ∼_MAX-equivalent to an earlier one (depth 2 and deeper); the specializations failing (1)–(6) factor through finitely many limit groups Red₁,…,Red_k, F_{R(V_{3,m_s})}, R_{Q1},…,R_{Qm}, H_surplus, whose NTQ groups are correcting extensions of the NTQ group of the sequence.
hypotheses: Data as in FO3/configuration-group; complete reducing systems computed by FO4/reducing-quotients-effective.
proofSteps: (1) Bound the widths by N of FO4/algebraic-solution-bound; for each width, the initial fundamental sequences modulo ⟨P⟩ are finitely many by FO2/fundamental-sequences-modulo.

(2) Build, for each system U_{2,m_s}, a generalized equation modulo ⟨P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾, Z₁^{(2,j,s)}⟩ for minimal algebraic solutions (bases moved to intervals labelled by parameters), glue in generalized equations for V_{2,m} and U_{1,m} along intervals with the same labels, and add the inequalities of (1)–(6) as non-identity conditions on bases (FG7/reduction-to-generalized-equations); construct their fundamental sequences modulo ⟨P⟩ with automorphism groups restricted to those preserving the generalized equations; the subgroups generated by the images of the generators in the terminal groups are the terminal groups for H.
(4) Classify how a generic family of the sequence can fail (1)–(6) and apply FO2/parametrization-theorem to see that the corresponding NTQ groups are correcting extensions.
acceptance: With t = 0 there is a single width and the depth-1 case occurs when algebraic solutions of U₁ form a generic family.

nodes.title: First step of the ∀∃-procedure: the free lift and the exceptional system U₀
nodes.statement: Let Φ = ∀X∃Y ⋁_i (U_i(X, Y) = 1 ∧ V_i(X, Y) ≠ 1) be a ∀∃-sentence of L_A in standard form (FO1/standard-form) over F = F(A), |A| ≥ 2. Run the equation–inequation solver of FreeGroupsAndLimitGroups FG7 over the free group F(A ⊔ X) on each disjunct, with Y as variables and X as constants. If no disjunct has a solution, return 'false'. Otherwise take the first solution Y = f(X) found, for a disjunct i, and set U₀(X) := V_i(X, f(X)): Φ holds at every X̄ with U₀(X̄) ≠ 1, and it remains to check the X̄ in V_F(U₀). If U₀ = 1 has no solution in F, return 'true' (the sentence is proved on the first level); otherwise pass G := F_{R(U₀)} with the set of all homomorphisms G → F to the root of the ∀∃-tree.
proofSteps: Solve U_i(X, Y) = 1 ∧ V_i(X, Y) ≠ 1 over F(A ⊔ X) with the solver of FG7 (decides and returns a solution).
No solution for any i: by FO1/free-lifting-theorem Φ is false.
A solution f for disjunct i: U_i(X, f(X)) = 1 identically, so Φ fails at most where V_i(X, f(X)) = 1; decide consistency of U₀ = 1 over F with the FG7 solver.
acceptance: For Φ = ∀x∃y (y = x), with standard form ∀x∃y (y x⁻¹ = 1 ∧ a ≠ 1), the first step returns 'true' with f(x) = x and U₀ = (a = 1), which is inconsistent over F.
For Φ = ∀x∃y (y² = x) the first step returns 'false'.

nodes.title: Block-NTQ groups and the minimality restriction
nodes.statement: Along a branch of the ∀∃-tree, let c be a fundamental sequence for G₁ modulo the images R₁,…,R_s of the free factors of ⟨X₂,…,X_n⟩, M(X, Z₁) the group generated by the top p levels of the NTQ group of c (above the level p where the projective image of G becomes proper, FO3/projective-images), c₃ the composite of the induced sequence c₂ for G above level p (FO3/induced-ntq) with a fundamental sequence b₂ for the quotient G_p, N̄₁ its canonical NTQ group and N̄₁corr a correcting extension relative to U(X, Y) = 1 ∧ V(X, Y) ≠ 1 (FO2/correcting-extension). The block-NTQ group N₁ is the fully residually free quotient of the amalgam of M(X, Z₁) and N̄₁corr along the top p levels of N̄₁corr, obtained by adding the relations that make it commutation transitive; it has two blocks, and later steps add blocks. The minimality restriction: the groups F_{R(U_{n+1})} carried by the next vertices are discriminated by homomorphisms minimal for N̄_n with respect to the images of G and minimal for the top block with respect to the images of the previous F_{R(U_n)}.
proofSteps: Form the amalgam M(X, Z₁) ∗_{top p levels} N̄₁corr from finite presentations.

Add commutation relations for pairs of elements whose centralizers must coincide (found with FG10/frf-basic-algorithms) until the group is commutation transitive; the result is fully residually free (FG8/frf-properties).
Record the blocks and their levels; state the minimality restriction through FO2/fundamental-sequences-modulo.
acceptance: If c has a single level identical to S₁ the block-NTQ group has a single block.
Every block-NTQ group is a finitely generated fully residually free group.

nodes.title: The ∀∃-tree T_EA(Φ)
nodes.statement: For a ∀∃-sentence Φ whose first step (FO5/ae-tree-first-step) passes G = F_{R(U₀)}, the tree T_EA(Φ) is built as follows. Root: all homomorphisms G → F. Level 1: one vertex for each well-aligned fundamental sequence V_fund(S(b)) of the canonical embedding tree of G (FO2/canonical-embedding-tree) with its correcting extension S_corr(b) (FO2/correcting-extension); if the image of G in N₀ = F_{R(S(b))} is a proper quotient, replace the vertex by the fundamental sequences of that quotient. Otherwise apply the parametrization theorem (FO2/parametrization-theorem) to get formula solutions Y = f(X₁,…,X_n) over S_corr(b) — if none exists, Φ is false; the construction searches for a formula solution and does not decide its existence — and restrict to values minimal with respect to the images of G (FO2/fundamental-sequences-modulo) satisfying the new equation V(X, f(X)) = 1, giving U₁ and G₁ = F_{R(U₁)}; if U₁ is inconsistent the branch is closed (proved on level 2). General step n: given the block-NTQ group N_{n−1} (FO5/block-ntq) and fundamental sequences c^{(n)} for G_n modulo the rigid subgroups R_{r(n)} of the top block: first easy case — G (or the current quotient) does not embed in the image of N_{n−1}: continue with the well-aligned sequences of the image G^{(n)}; second easy case — some top block M_{g(r)}(X, Z_{g(r)}) has a proper projective image: restart from vertex w_{g(r)+1} with that quotient and only sequences of non-maximal complexity; Case 1 (top levels agree: pass to the next level), Case 2 (top levels of c^{(n−1)},…,c^{(n−i)} agree but not c^{(n)}: a level where the image of the top block is proper; build the next blocks from the induced sequence and a sequence for the quotient), Case 3 (consecutive top levels differ: likewise, with sequences not of maximal complexity), Case 4 (all levels agree: replace c by the sequence d induced by the image G_{n,corr} of the corrective extension, which decreases the number of free factors, the regular size or the abelian size at some level). Each vertex carries a fundamental sequence, a block-NTQ group, a correcting extension and, after the parametrization theorem, the next equation. The construction halts when Φ is true (FO5/ae-tree-correct); when Φ is false it may not halt, and the decider (FO5/ae-decider) runs it alongside a search for a counterexample.
proofSteps: Implement the tree as a finitely branching tree whose vertices hold finite presentations of block-NTQ groups, fundamental sequences and equations; every operation used is one of the effective constructions of FO2–FO3 and FG10.
At each vertex decide which case applies (properness of projective images is decidable, FO3/projective-images) and apply it.

Formula solutions are found by search, not decided: enumerate tuples Y of words in the generators of the correcting extension F_{R(Ū)} and test W(X^θ, Y) = 1 and W₁(X^θ, Y) ≠ 1 with the word problem of FG10/frf-basic-algorithms-correct. When Φ is true a formula solution exists at every vertex (FO2/parametrization-theorem; IFT Theorem 12 finds it effectively), so each search halts. When Φ is false a search may run forever, and falsity is detected by the counterexample search of FO5/ae-decider. (Deciding the existence of formula solutions outright would need equations with inequations over the limit group F_{R(Ū)}, FG10/equations-over-limit-groups, which rests on a recorded gap of FreeGroupsAndLimitGroups and is not used here.)
A branch is closed when its current equation is inconsistent over F (decided by FG7/solver-procedure); the construction returns 'true' when every branch is closed.

For Φ = ∀x∃y (y ≠ 1 ∧ [x, y] = 1) the tree closes on level 2.

nodes.title: Finiteness of the ∀∃-tree
nodes.statement: For every ∀∃-sentence Φ of L_A over F = F(A), |A| ≥ 2, the tree T_EA(Φ) (FO5/ae-tree) is finite and its construction terminates. The proof is by induction on the length of the longest proper descending chain of fully residually free quotients of G and on the complexity of the top level S₁ (FO3/complexity): in Case 3 the complexity of the top block decreases (by Lemma 2: the homomorphisms through c are generic for each regular quadratic equation of Q₁ and ab(c) = ab(V_fund(Q)), so c has one level identical to Q₁; or S can be rebuilt with smaller size; or sizes agree and ab(c) < ab(V_fund(Q))); the second easy case can recur only finitely often for each r (descending chain of proper quotients of M_{g(r)}); Case 4 cannot recur with N_n = N_{n₁} forever; the first easy case and Case 2 pass to proper quotients, finite by induction.
hypotheses: F = F(A), |A| ≥ 2; Φ a ∀∃-sentence of L_A.
proofSteps: Proper descending chains of fully residually free quotients of a finitely generated fully residually free group are finite (equational Noetherianity, FG5/FG8): this bounds the first easy case and Case 2.

Lemma 2: for a sequence c modulo the free factors of ⟨X₂,…,X_m⟩ with the same Kurosh rank as Q₁, either c is generic for each regular quadratic equation of Q₁ with ab(c) = ab(V_fund(Q)) (one level identical to Q₁), or S can be rebuilt with size(S) < size(Q₁), or size(S) = size(Q₁) and ab(c) < ab(V_fund(Q)) (uses FO2/generic-family-lifts and stability of QH subgroups).
Hence Case 3 decreases the well-founded complexity of the top block, so it applies finitely often; then the procedure moves to the second block, finite by induction.
acceptance: For a sentence proved on the first level the tree has one vertex.

nodes.title: Correctness of the ∀∃-tree: both answers
nodes.statement: Let Φ = ∀X∃Y φ₀ be a ∀∃-sentence of L_A over F = F(A), |A| ≥ 2. (1) If the construction of T_EA(Φ) ends with every branch closed (every terminal equation inconsistent over F), Φ is true in F. (2) If at some vertex no formula solution exists over the correcting extension (in particular if the first step finds no free lift), Φ is false in F. (3) If Φ is true, the construction, with formula solutions found by search, halts with every branch closed. (4) Φ is false iff there is X̄ ∈ F^X at which the universal sentence ∀Y ¬φ₀(X̄, Y), with constants from F, holds in F.
proofSteps: (1) Every X̄ ∈ F^X is either verified at some vertex (the formula solution witnesses Φ at X̄) or factors through an open vertex (AETree.homs_cover); closed branches have no remaining X̄, so all X̄ are verified.

Minimality: if a specialization of the variables of the fundamental sequence is replaced by a minimal one in its class, Φ at X̄ is unchanged, since the classes are orbits of canonical automorphisms fixing the images of G (QE-FREE p. 12).

(2) If Φ were true, the parametrization theorem (FO2/parametrization-theorem) would give a formula solution at every vertex, applied to the NTQ system of the vertex restricted to the remaining X; at the first step this is FO1/free-lifting-theorem.

(3) If Φ is true, by (2) a formula solution exists at every vertex, so every search halts; the construction is finite (FO5/ae-tree-finite), so it ends, and since no vertex lacks a formula solution every branch ends closed.
(4) is the meaning of the falsity of ∀X∃Y φ₀; the universal sentences ∀Y ¬φ₀(X̄, Y) with constants from F are decided by FG7/existential-universal-deciders.
acceptance: ∀x∃y (y ≠ 1 ∧ [x, y] = 1) gives (1) and (3); ∀x∃y ([x, y] ≠ 1) gives (2) at the vertex x = 1 and (4) with X̄ = 1.

nodes.title: The decider for ∀∃-sentences
nodes.statement: aeDecide takes (the FG3 code of) a ∀∃-sentence Φ = ∀X∃Y φ₀ of L_A and runs two searches in parallel, returning the first answer: (a) the standard form (FO1/standard-form) and the first step (FO5/ae-tree-first-step), returning false if no free lift exists, and then the construction of T_EA(Φ) (FO5/ae-tree), returning true when every branch is closed; (b) an enumeration of tuples X̄ ∈ F^X, returning false at the first X̄ for which FG7's universal decider confirms ∀Y ¬φ₀(X̄, Y). Equivalently, the true ∀∃-sentences and the false ones are both recursively enumerable, and Post's theorem (Mathlib's ComputablePred.computable_iff_re_compl_re') makes truth a computable predicate. On an ∃∀-sentence Ψ it returns the negation of aeDecide on the ∀∃-sentence equivalent to ¬Ψ (FO1/quantifier-classes).
proofSteps: Compose the computable steps (FG3 encodings, FO1 standard form, FG7 solver and universal decider, FO2–FO3 constructions, FG10 algorithms).

Search (a) halts on true sentences (FO5/ae-tree-correct (3)) and its answer true is correct (FO5/ae-tree-correct (1)); its answer false at the first step is correct by FO1/free-lifting-theorem. Search (b) halts on false sentences (FO5/ae-tree-correct (4)) and its answer is correct. So both answers are correct and one search always halts.
In Mathlib's terms: truth is REPred through (a), falsity is REPred through (b), and ComputablePred.computable_iff_re_compl_re' gives the total computable decider.

The set of ∀∃-sentences of L_A (with constants from F(A)) true in F(A) is decidable: the predicate Φ ↦ (F(A) ⊨ Φ) on the Primcodable type of codes of ∀∃-sentences (FG3/effective-encoding) is a ComputablePred, decided by aeDecide with correctness of both answers (FO5/ae-tree-correct). Consequently the set of ∃∀-sentences true in F(A) is decidable.

nodes.title: Sacerdote's theorem: nonabelian free groups have the same ∀∃-theory
nodes.statement: A coefficient-free ∀∃-sentence of the language of groups holds in one nonabelian free group of finite rank iff it holds in every one; hence all nonabelian free groups of finite rank satisfy the same Boolean combinations of coefficient-free ∀∃-sentences. In this roadmap's route it follows from the construction of the ∀∃-tree: for a coefficient-free sentence every object built along T_EA(Φ) (canonical Makanin–Razborov diagrams, fundamental sequences, correcting extensions, formula solutions) is coefficient-free and the same for F_k and F_ℓ, k, ℓ ≥ 2, up to replacing each terminal factor L by L ∗ F_{ℓ−k}.
hypotheses: Coefficient-free sentences only (with constants the statement compares F(A) with F(A ⊔ B), FO7/elementary-embedding).
proofSteps: For a coefficient-free Φ, work with the coefficient-free general standard form (FO1/standard-form (1)) and keep every construction coefficient-free: the merged form (2) introduces the constants a, b and is not used, and a coefficient-free replacement for the merging of equations and inequations is part of the recorded gap 'rank independence in KM's route'. The first step then solves coefficient-free systems over F_k ∗ F(X) with X as constants; solvability does not depend on k ≥ 2, because F_k ∗ F(X) and F_ℓ ∗ F(X) embed in each other over F(X) and existential formulas with constants from F(X) go up along embeddings.

Each later construction (canonical embedding tree, correcting extensions, parametrization) for a coefficient-free system over F_ℓ is obtained from that over F_k by replacing terminal factors L by L ∗ F_{ℓ−k} (SELA-VI p. 5).
So the trees for F_k and F_ℓ close or fail at the same vertices, and by FO5/ae-tree-correct Φ has the same truth value.
acceptance: The universal sentence ∀x∀y ([x, y] = 1) fails in every nonabelian free group.

nodes.title: The bound on algebraic solutions is computable
nodes.statement: In FO4/algebraic-solution-bound the constant N(K, H) can be computed from finite presentations of K and generators of H. nodes.title: The parametric ∀∃-tree T_X(Θ) of an ∃∀∃-formula
nodes.statement: Let Θ(P) = ∃Z∀X∃Y ⋁_i (U_i(A, P, Z, X, Y) = 1 ∧ V_i(A, P, Z, X, Y) ≠ 1) be an L_A-formula with parameters P (QE-FREE writes the case of one disjunct, the negation of the ∀∃∀ form of KM06). For every P̄, Z̄ at which ∀X∃Y(…) holds there is a free lift Y = f(A, P̄, Z̄, X) in F(X) ∗ F (FO1/free-lifting-theorem); all such formula solutions for all values of the parameters lie in finitely many fundamental sequences whose terminal groups are F_{R(U_{1,i})} ∗ F(X), U_{1,i} = U_{1,i}(A, P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾), with F_{R(U_{1,i})} without sufficient splitting modulo ⟨A, P, Z⟩ (FO2/fundamental-sequences-modulo). For each, the values (P, Z) admitting X with V(P, Z, X, f) = 1 for all such f form an equation over F_{R(U_{1,i})} ∗ F(X), equivalent to finitely many (one, with constants) equations, with coordinate group G and fully residually free quotients G_i. T_X(Θ) is built like T_EA (FO5/ae-tree) with X, Y as variables and P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾ as parameters: fundamental sequences of the G_i modulo ⟨P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾⟩ with terminal groups F_{R(V_{2,i})} (no sufficient splitting modulo ⟨P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾⟩), formula solutions of U = 1 in their correcting extensions (FO2/parametrization-theorem), described by fundamental sequences with terminal groups F_{R(U_{2,i})}, and so on. Each branch carries F_{R(U_{1,i})}, F_{R(V_{2,i})}, …, F_{R(V_{r,i})}, F_{R(U_{r,i})}; F_{R(U_{m,i})} has no sufficient splitting modulo ⟨P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾, Z₁⁽ᵐ⁾⟩ and F_{R(V_{m,i})} none modulo ⟨P, Z, Z⁽¹⁾⟩. The tree is finite and can be constructed effectively, together with a fundamental sequence at each vertex describing Y (at the groups F_{R(U_{j,i})}) or X (at the groups F_{R(V_{j,i})}).
proofSteps: Top: the formula solutions of U = 1 ∧ V ≠ 1 for all parameter values lie in finitely many fundamental sequences modulo ⟨A, P, Z⟩ (FO1/free-lifting-theorem with FO2/fundamental-sequences-modulo).
The remaining X: the condition V(P, Z, X, f) = 1 for every f of the sequence is a system over F_{R(U_{1,i})} ∗ F(X), equivalent to a finite subsystem by equational Noetherianity (FG5).

The formula solutions of U = 1 over the correcting extensions of the NTQ groups at level m ≥ 2 are all of them, not one: QE-FREE p. 27 describes the set of all formula solutions Y by finitely many fundamental sequences. That set is the solution set of an equation over a finitely generated fully residually free group, and its description is a complete Hom-diagram over that group (FG10/equations-over-limit-groups), which rests on a recorded gap of FreeGroupsAndLimitGroups (gap 'all formula solutions over NTQ groups').

Continue as in FO5/ae-tree with the parameter subgroups; finiteness by the argument of FO5/ae-tree-finite; the algorithm uses FO4/reducing-quotients-effective and fundamental sequences modulo subgroups (QE-FREE Proposition 4).

nodes.title: The sets True(Θ)_m: parameters verified at level m
nodes.statement: For Θ(P) and its parametric tree T_X(Θ) (FO6/parametric-tree), a proof that ∀X∃Y(U(P̄, Z̄, X, Y) = 1 ∧ V ≠ 1) holds is a true-subtree of T_X(Θ): a finite sequence of formula solutions Y in correcting extensions of the block-NTQ groups at its vertices, verifying the sentence at every X̄; there are finitely many possible true-subtrees, and the sentence for (P̄, Z̄) is proved at level m when the maximal depth of a true-subtree for it is m. True(Θ)_m is the set of P̄ for which some Z̄ has its sentence proved at level m: there are solutions of some U_{m,j} = 1 but no remaining X at level m, i.e. no solution of V_{m+1,j} = 1. True(Θ) = {P̄ | F ⊨ Θ(P̄)} = ⋃_{m ≤ depth} True(Θ)_m.
proofSteps: Define true-subtrees as subtrees of the finite tree T_X(Θ) with formula-solution data; there are finitely many.
Define True(Θ)_m as the projection to P of the tuples (P̄, Z̄, Z̄⁽¹⁾, …) admitting a true-subtree of depth exactly m.
True(Θ) is their finite union because the tree has bounded depth.
acceptance: True(Θ)_1 for Θ proved on the first level is the set of P̄ with an algebraic Z⁽¹⁾ on some U_{1,i} and no V_{2,j}-solution.
If T_X(Θ) has depth 1, True(Θ) = True(Θ)_1.

The absence of solutions of the finitely many V_{2,j} is universal; the existence of Z, Z⁽¹⁾ is existential: the conjunction is ∃∀.

nodes.title: True(Θ)₂ is a Boolean combination of ∃∀-sets, effectively
nodes.statement: True(Θ)₂ is defined by a Boolean combination of ∃∀-formulas in P that can be computed from Θ. Proof plan: for each of the finitely many initial fundamental sequences of level 2 and width i (FO3/configuration-finiteness), P̄ is in True(Θ)₂ through that sequence at depth 1 iff (a) there are algebraic solutions of a system U_{i,coeff} = 1 attached to the terminal group of a fundamental sequence of a configuration group modulo P, (b) these do not factor through the finitely many fundamental sequences of Red₁,…,Red_k, F_{R(V_{3,m_s})}, R_{Q1},…,R_{Qm}, H_surplus, and (c) they do not factor through the terminal groups of the deeper sequences of level 2; each condition is a Boolean combination of conjunctive ∃∀-formulas. Deeper sequences (depth 2, 3, …) are constructed with tight enveloping fundamental sequences (FO3/tight-enveloping); their complexity does not increase from depth n to n + 1 and cannot stay equal for more than a computable number of steps (FO3/tight-envelope-reorganization and the computable bound of KM06 Lemma 28), so the construction stops.
hypotheses: Θ an ∃∀∃-formula; all data computed by FO6/parametric-tree.
proofSteps: For each initial fundamental sequence f of level 2 and width i (finitely many, computable: FO3/configuration-finiteness), write (a)–(c) at depth 1 using algebraicity and MAX-class counts (FO4/max-class-count-definable) and the computable bound (FO5/effective-bound).
If the depth-1 criterion fails because certificates extend through H_surplus, build the depth-2 sequences from tight enveloping sequences (FO3/tight-enveloping) and repeat.

Termination: the complexity of the depth-(n + 1) sequence is at most that of depth n and equality persists for a bounded, computable number of steps (FO3/tight-envelope-reorganization); the bound is effective by QE-FREE Proposition 7(2).
True(Θ)₂ is the union over sequences and depths of the resulting Boolean combinations.
acceptance: If T_X(Θ) has depth 1, True(Θ)₂ = ∅.

nodes.title: Elimination of an ∃∀∃-block to a Boolean combination of ∃∀-formulas

Namely elimEAE Θ is the disjunction over m ≤ depth T_X(Θ) of the Boolean combinations of FO6/true-all-levels.

proofSteps: Compute T_X(Θ) and its depth r (FO6/parametric-tree).
For each m ≤ r compute the Boolean combination β_m defining True(Θ)_m (FO6/true-all-levels).
Return β₁ ∨ ⋯ ∨ β_r; correctness is FO6/true-sets (trueSet_eq_iUnion).

nodes.title: The termination measure: number of alternating quantifier blocks
nodes.statement: For an L_A-formula φ, blocks(φ) is the number k of ∀∃-pairs in its standard form ∀X₁∃Y₁…∀X_k∃Y_k ψ (FO1/standard-form), ψ quantifier-free; formulas with blocks(φ) ≤ 1 are ∀∃-formulas. blocks takes values in ℕ, ordered by <.
proofSteps: Define blocks as the k of stdForm φ; a quantifier-free formula has blocks 0.

Prove blocks (∀X∃Y ψ) = blocks ψ + 1 when ψ is in standard form, and that every Boolean combination of ∀∃-formulas has blocks at most 2 (renaming bound variables apart, it prenexes to an ∃∀∃-formula, whose standard form is ∀∅∃Z∀X∃Y θ).

nodes.title: The outer quantifier-elimination procedure
nodes.statement: qeAE is defined by recursion on blocks (FO6/qe-measure). Given φ(P), compute stdForm φ = ∀X₁∃Y₁ ψ(P, X₁, Y₁) with blocks ψ = blocks φ − 1. If blocks φ ≤ 1 return φ (a ∀∃-formula). Otherwise let β(P, X₁, Y₁) := qeAE ψ, a Boolean combination of ∀∃-formulas. Then ∃Y₁ β: put β in disjunctive normal form over ∀∃- and ∃∀-formulas (negated ∀∃-formulas, FO1/quantifier-classes); ∃Y₁ distributes over ∨, and each ∃Y₁(α₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ ε₁ ∧ ⋯) with α_j ∀∃ and ε_j ∃∀ is, after renaming bound variables apart (FG3/syntax-operations-computable), an ∃∀∃-formula in (P, X₁); apply elimEAE (FO6/eae-elimination) to get a Boolean combination γ(P, X₁) of ∃∀-formulas. Finally ∀X₁ γ = ¬∃X₁ ¬γ: rewrite ¬γ in disjunctive normal form, eliminate ∃X₁ the same way, and negate. The result is a Boolean combination of ∀∃-formulas in P.
proofSteps: Recursion on blocks φ; the recursive call is on ψ with blocks ψ = blocks φ − 1.
Disjunctive normal form over the atoms 'α ∀∃' and 'ε ∃∀' is a primitive recursive syntactic operation; conjunctions of prenex formulas are prenexed by renaming bound variables apart (FG3).
Two calls of elimEAE per round (for ∃Y₁ and, after negation, for ∃X₁).
acceptance: qeAE φ = φ for every ∀∃-formula.
For φ = ∀x∃y∀z∃w θ, one round reduces to elimination of ∃∀∃-formulas.

nodes.title: Tarski's decidability theorem for free groups
nodes.statement: Let A be finite with |A| ≥ 2. The elementary theory of F(A) with constants from A is decidable: the predicate σ ↦ (FreeGroup A ⊨ σ) on codes of L_A-sentences (FG3/effective-encoding) is a ComputablePred, decided by decideTh (FO7/decision-procedure) with correctness of both answers. In particular the coefficient-free elementary theory of a nonabelian free group of finite rank is decidable.
hypotheses: A finite with |A| ≥ 2.
proofSteps: decideTh σ = true iff qeAE σ evaluates to true under aeDecide iff F(A) ⊨ qeAE σ (FO5/ae-decidable) iff F(A) ⊨ σ (FO6/qe-procedure-correct).
decideTh is computable (FO7/decision-procedure).
acceptance: The theory decides Vaught's sentence (true) and ∃x (x² = a) (false).

nodes.title: Coefficient-free elimination is uniform in the rank
nodes.statement: For every coefficient-free formula φ(P) of the language of groups there is a coefficient-free Boolean combination ψ of coefficient-free ∀∃-formulas, computed from φ by the coefficient-free run of the elimination (FO6/qe-procedure with the general standard form of FO1/standard-form (1), no constants introduced, and every diagram, correcting extension, induced and tight enveloping system and configuration built for coefficient-free systems), such that φ ∼_{F_k} ψ for every k ≥ 2: the same Boolean combination defines the set of φ in every nonabelian free group of finite rank. (qeAE run over F(A) with the merged standard form may introduce the constants a, b, so it does not by itself give this statement.)
hypotheses: φ coefficient-free; k ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Every object built along the parametric trees for a coefficient-free formula is coefficient-free: Makanin–Razborov diagrams of coefficient-free systems over F_k are obtained from those over F₂ by replacing terminal factors L by L ∗ F_{k−2} (SELA-VI pp. 3–5), and the same holds for correcting extensions, induced and tight enveloping NTQ systems and configurations. The merging of equations and inequations in FO1/standard-form (2) uses the constants a, b; the coefficient-free run keeps finite systems or merges them by a coefficient-free device (part of the gap 'rank independence in KM's route').
Hence the coefficient-free run does not depend on k ≥ 2, and its correctness (FO6/qe-procedure-correct, applied to the coefficient-free run) holds over each F_k.
acceptance: For φ quantifier-free the coefficient-free run returns φ (as a Boolean combination of its atomic formulas).

By FO5/ae-rank-independence each ∀∃-constituent of ψ has the same truth value in F_k and F_ℓ; so does ψ, hence σ (Mathlib's elementarilyEquivalent_iff).

nodes.title: The standard embedding F_k → F_ℓ is elementary
nodes.statement: For 2 ≤ k ≤ ℓ the standard embedding FreeGroup (Fin k) → FreeGroup (Fin ℓ) induced by Fin.castLE (FreeGroup.map) is an elementary embedding in Mathlib's sense (ElementaryEmbedding for the language of groups). More generally, for a nonabelian free group F₁ and any free group F₂, F₁ → F₁ ∗ F₂ is elementary; equivalently, for L_A-formulas with constants from A, the free group F(A) is an elementary subgroup of F(A ⊔ B).

nodes.title: Extended hyperbolic floors and towers
nodes.statement: A graph of groups with surfaces is a graph of groups (FG4/graph-of-groups) in which some vertices are of surface type: their vertex group is the fundamental group of a compact connected surface Σ with boundary, with the incident edge groups being exactly the maximal boundary subgroups (one edge per boundary component), with a Bass–Serre presentation (T¹, T⁰). A triple (G, G′, r) with G′ ≤ G and r : G → G′ a retraction is an extended hyperbolic floor if G has a non-trivial decomposition Γ as a graph of groups with surfaces such that: the surfaces of Γ other than once-punctured tori have Euler characteristic ≤ −2; G′ is the free product of the stabilizers of the non-surface-type vertices of T⁰; every edge joins a surface-type vertex to a non-surface-type vertex; and either r sends every surface-type vertex group to a non-abelian image (a hyperbolic floor), or G′ is cyclic and there is a retraction r′ : G ∗ ℤ → G′ ∗ ℤ sending surface-type vertex groups to non-abelian images. A non-cyclic group G is an extended hyperbolic tower over a subgroup H if there are G = G₀ ≥ G₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ G_m ≥ H (m ≥ 0) with each (G_k, G_{k+1}, r_k) an extended hyperbolic floor in which H lies in a non-surface-type vertex group, and G_m = H ∗ F ∗ S₁ ∗ ⋯ ∗ S_p with F free (possibly trivial) and each S_i the fundamental group of a closed surface of Euler characteristic ≤ −2.
proofSteps: Define graphs of groups with surfaces on top of FG4's graphs of groups and FG6's surface groups with boundary (peripheral structure from FG6/qh-vertex).
Define ExtendedHyperbolicFloor G G′ r and IsExtendedHyperbolicTower G H as in the statement; the Euler characteristic is FG6's χ.
Record the special cases: m = 0 gives G = H ∗ F ∗ S₁ ∗ ⋯ ∗ S_p.

nodes.title: Finitely generated groups elementarily equivalent to a free group
nodes.statement: A finitely generated group G is elementarily equivalent (in the language of groups, without constants) to a nonabelian free group of finite rank iff G is an extended hyperbolic tower over the trivial subgroup (FO7/hyperbolic-tower). By FO7/elementary-equivalence the condition does not depend on the rank of the free group.
hypotheses: G finitely generated.
proofSteps: If: a tower is built from a base H ∗ F ∗ S₁ ∗ ⋯ ∗ S_p by floors with retractions; each floor is a regular quadratic level over the lower floor in the sense of FG6/FG8, so the tower is an NTQ group with generic families (FO2/ntq-generic-family), and the elimination (FO6) and the parametrization theorem (FO2) show that every ∀∃-sentence and then every sentence true in F holds in G (SELA-VI Theorem 7 and its proof, p. 14 onward, for Sela's towers). For extended floors whose lower floor is cyclic, LPS Remark 3.7 and PERIN p. 17 report on Sela's authority that the proof extends; no written proof is available (gap 'the if direction for extended floors').

Only if: G is a non-elementary hyperbolic limit group (FO7/necessary-conditions); its cyclic JSJ decomposition (FG10/jsj-existence) must contain QH vertex groups (the argument of SELA-VI Claim 5); a non-injective preretraction obtained from the Makanin–Razborov diagram of G (FG10) by first-order sentences true in F (SELA-VI Proposition 6 and its proof, pp. 9–14) gives, by Perin's corrected Proposition 5.11 (PERIN, statement p. 19, proof §7, pp. 31–47), a retraction onto a proper subgroup forming an extended hyperbolic floor; induction on the subgroup (descending chains of limit-group quotients) gives the tower.

nodes.title: Necessary conditions: a f.g. model is a non-elementary hyperbolic limit group without ℤ²
nodes.statement: If a finitely generated group G is elementarily equivalent to a nonabelian free group F, then: (1) G has the same universal theory as F, hence is a limit group (finitely generated fully residually free, FG8/limit-group-equivalences) and is non-abelian; (2) G contains no subgroup isomorphic to ℤ²: the sentence 'for every x ≠ 1 the centralizer C(x) has at most two cosets of its subgroup of squares', ∀x∀y₁∀y₂∀y₃ (x ≠ 1 ∧ ⋀_i [x, y_i] = 1 → ⋁_{i<j} ∃z ([x, z] = 1 ∧ y_i y_j⁻¹ = z²)), holds in F, where C(x) is infinite cyclic; in a limit group the centralizer of x ≠ 1 is free abelian of finite rank, so a subgroup ℤ² ∋ x gives C(x) ≅ ℤ^r with r ≥ 2 and 2^r ≥ 4 cosets of squares (SELA-VI p. 7 counts classes of commuting elements mod 2); (3) consequently G is a non-elementary torsion-free hyperbolic group.
hypotheses: G finitely generated.
proofSteps: (1) Elementary equivalence gives the same universal theory; by FG8/limit-group-equivalences (with Remeslennikov's theorem in FG5/FG8) G is fully residually free.

(2) The displayed sentence holds in F because centralizers of non-trivial elements are infinite cyclic (FreeGroupsAndLimitGroups FG1/centralizer-cyclic). By (1) G is a limit group, whose centralizers of non-trivial elements are abelian and free abelian of finite rank (FG8/frf-properties (1), (3)); a subgroup ℤ² ≤ G and x ≠ 1 in it give C(x) ≅ ℤ^r, r ≥ 2, with at least four cosets of squares, so G fails the sentence (SELA-VI p. 7).

(3) A limit group without ℤ² is hyperbolic (limit groups are toral relatively hyperbolic; with no non-cyclic abelian subgroups they are hyperbolic), and it is non-elementary because it is non-abelian (FG8/frf-properties).
acceptance: ℤ² and F₂ × ℤ are not models.
Every f.g. model is torsion-free and CSA.

nodes.title: Groups that are not elementarily equivalent to a free group
nodes.statement: None of the following is elementarily equivalent to F₂: (a) the closed non-orientable surface group of genus 3, N₃ = ⟨x, y, z | x²y²z²⟩: Vaught's universal sentence ∀x∀y∀z (x²y²z² = 1 → [x, y] = 1 ∧ [x, z] = 1 ∧ [y, z] = 1) holds in every free group (Lyndon) and fails in N₃ (its generators do not pairwise commute, as N₃ is non-abelian); (b) the double F ∗_{⟨w⟩} F = ⟨b₁, b₂⟩ ∗_{w(b₁,b₂) = w(b₃,b₄)} ⟨b₃, b₄⟩ of F₂ along an element w without roots, when this amalgam is its abelian JSJ decomposition; (c) any group containing ℤ², for instance ℤ² and F₂ × ℤ; (d) abelian groups, for instance ℤ (the sentence ∀x∀y [x, y] = 1).
hypotheses: In (b), w has no proper roots in F₂ and the amalgam is the abelian JSJ decomposition of the double.
proofSteps: (a) In F, x²y²z² = 1 forces pairwise commutation (Lyndon; the radical of x₁²x₂²x₃² = 1 in FG6/quadratic-radicals); in N₃ the generators satisfy x²y²z² = 1 but do not all commute (N₃ is non-abelian, χ = −1).

(b) Follow SELA-VI Claim 5: write the system Σ of the presentation, view it over F and over G; over F every solution can be moved by the modular group into one of the finitely many proper quotients G₁,…,G_ℓ, which is a coefficient-free AE sentence; over G the tautological solution cannot be so moved since the modular group of G is cyclic (generated by the Dehn twist along w).
(c), (d) FO7/necessary-conditions; for ℤ the sentence ∀x∀y [x, y] = 1.
acceptance: Vaught's sentence separates N₃ from F₂; ∀x∀y [x, y] = 1 separates ℤ from F₂.
